description: Baseline synthetic marginals and a common-shock share of 0.30. Contract rules are unchanged. Not an official benchmark.
Shared-shock weight is zero. Country occurrence probabilities match the baseline. Not an official benchmark.
Shared-shock weight is 0.80 of the smaller marginal. Marginals match the baseline. Not an official benchmark.
Precipitation occurrence is multiplied by 1.75. The common-shock share stays 0.30, so the shared-shock probability rises with the marginals.
Either precipitation severity pays the full precipitation principal, still once per term.
Occurrence rates are scaled down to 8 percent of baseline. This is a quiet book, not a literal zero-hazard world, because a zero probability is outside the scenario bounds.
Earthquakes keep baseline rates and are independent across countries. Precipitation is scaled to a residual 8 percent.
Precipitation keeps baseline rates and is independent across countries. Earthquake occurrence is scaled to a residual 8 percent.
Earthquake occurrence is 1.35 times baseline. Dependence and precipitation stay at the baseline settings.
Earthquake occurrence is 2.10 times baseline and the common-shock share is raised to 0.45.
Precipitation occurrence is 2.40 times baseline. The common-shock share is 0.40.
Earthquake rates are raised and 90 percent of the smaller marginal is a shared shock. Precipitation is residual.
Precipitation rates are raised and 90 percent of the smaller marginal is a shared shock. Earthquake occurrence is residual.
Both hazards are scaled by 1.50 and the common-shock share is 0.50. The hazards remain independent of each other.
Common-shock share is only 0.10 of the smaller marginal. Marginals match the baseline.
Common-shock share is 0.95 of the smaller marginal. Marginals match the baseline, so expected loss is unchanged while joint payout risk rises.
Both hazards are 1.20 times baseline, with the baseline common-shock share.
Earthquake occurrence is 1.90 times baseline, precipitation 1.70 times, and the common-shock share is 0.55.
A low-frequency tail is represented by sharply higher occurrence and a 0.85 common-shock share. Still a synthetic rate, not a forecast.
Highest occurrence scales in the library, a full common shock, and full precipitation steps. The smaller country's idiosyncratic shock is zero.
Same portfolio as the baseline, scored at a 10 million USD threshold instead of 25 million. Expected loss does not change. Exceedance and stop-loss do.
Kyrgyz occurrence is 1.75 times baseline for both hazards. Tajik rates are unchanged.
Tajik occurrence is 1.75 times baseline for both hazards. Kyrgyz rates are unchanged.
Principals, caps and insured exposure are 55 percent of the baseline. Hazard rates are unchanged.
Insured limit is concentrated in the Kyrgyz earthquake tower: 110 million earthquake principal against a much smaller Tajik book.
Steps stay below the principal: earthquake 10/25/45 percent and precipitation 25/55 percent.
Any positive severity pays the full peril principal, still subject to the caps and the term aggregation.
Occurrence is raised, the common shock is 0.90, precipitation steps are full, and the country cap equals the earthquake cap.
